chunks: And to set your face toward the way, as one upright, and not be one of those who associate others with God.

key_terms.الدِّينِ: The religion, specifically Islam as the way of life
key_terms.الْمُشْرِكِينَ: Those who associate partners with God

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to set one's face toward the religion as hanif?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the Prophet Muhammad and Imam Ali as the ultimate exemplars of the 'Hanif' faith, representing a pure, unadulterated monotheism that predates later sectarian divisions. The command to 'establish your face' implies a comprehensive orientation of one’s entire being—intellect, will, and action—towards divine unity, serving as a foundational principle for avoiding both major and minor forms of shirk.
